lessons.title: Roles and collaboration
objectives: Prepare a clear handover without inventing an organization chart.
explanation: No current approved AITS organization chart was located in the inspected materials. This lesson therefore describes functions, not confirmed departments or reporting lines. In a typical service business, customer-facing staff capture requirements, technical staff assess feasibility, administration maintains records, and an authorized reviewer confirms commercial or operational decisions.

A useful handover states the request, known facts, open questions, relevant evidence and next action. It identifies who is being asked to respond without assuming authority they do not have. Ask your supervisor to confirm actual role names and escalation routes. A handover is incomplete when the recipient cannot tell what decision is needed.
lessons.example: Synthetic ticket LH-001 says “camera problem.” A better handover says “Entrance camera image missing since 09:00; other views work; model and safe observations attached; technical diagnosis requested.”
lessons.exercise: Rewrite “customer unhappy, please fix” as a five-field handover.
lessons.model_response: Request: restore entrance view. Facts: missing since 09:00. Evidence: authorized screenshot without people. Unknown: power status. Next action: technical review and agreed update time.
key_points: Functional map is not an organization chart

lessons.title: Learning Hub and your first learning cycle
objectives: Complete a lesson, attempt a quiz and distinguish practice from approval.
explanation: Open the Learning Hub with your assigned account, select an assigned course and read the lesson objectives. Work through the explanation and exercise before taking the quiz. objectives: Separate legal minimums from unverified AITS arrangements.

lessons.title: Hours rest and holidays
objectives: Recognize the ordinary statutory baseline and its limits.
explanation: For ordinary work, Ministry of Labour guidance describes normal limits of eight hours a day and 48 hours a week, with lawful arrangements and sector exceptions requiring review. Specified hazardous work has a seven-hour daily and 42-hour weekly limit. The ordinary rest rule provides at least one hour after no more than five consecutive working hours; agreed split breaks and statutory exceptions must be checked.

The general baseline includes at least one weekly holiday with no more than six days between, at least 13 traditional holidays including National Labour Day, and at least six working days of annual holiday after one continuous year. These are legal baselines, not a statement of the AITS roster. Overtime consent, exceptions and pay should be checked separately; do not infer that a customer deadline overrides them.
lessons.example: A fictional roster appears to schedule continuous work without a break. Identify the concern and ask HR to check the actual arrangement and exceptions.
lessons.exercise: Annotate a sample 09:00–18:00 schedule with a one-hour midday break, then list what remains unknown.
lessons.model_response: Eight working hours are shown. Weekly total, holiday arrangements, actual duties and any overtime remain to be verified.

objectives: Review power compatibility and cabling before connection.
explanation: Power over Ethernet can deliver power and data over compatible Ethernet cabling. Check both the device’s supported PoE type and the switch or injector’s capability. Complaints and professional communication

Sample Content — Pending Company Approval

Version 0.1.0 | AITS-C06-L02 | Draft | 15 minutes

Learning objective

Acknowledge a complaint and agree a next step without unsupported promises.

Explanation

Listen without interrupting, summarize the issue and acknowledge its impact. Ask focused questions to establish what happened and what outcome the customer seeks. Avoid assigning blame before evidence is available. A respectful acknowledgement can be accurate without admitting an unverified cause or promising compensation.

Record the complaint, impact, evidence available, agreed contact method and next update. Escalate to the authorized responsible function when the request exceeds your role. Do not invent a refund rule or service deadline. If language becomes abusive or safety is threatened, seek the applicable supervisor/site response instead of escalating the confrontation.

Synthetic example

Cedar Office reports that a missed appointment interrupted work. “I understand this disrupted your schedule. I will record the details and ask the responsible team to confirm the next step.”

Practical exercise

Draft a complaint response containing acknowledgement, clarification and a realistic next action.

Model response

I understand the disruption. Please confirm the appointment reference and what occurred. I will ask the responsible team to review it and agree the next update with you.

Summary

Acknowledge impact Clarify facts without blame Agree the next update

lessons.title: Evidence and deviations
objectives: Record actual results and disclose departures from the plan.
explanation: Evidence connects a requirement to an observed result. Record what was checked, the method, time, relevant identifier and result. “Done” alone is weak evidence when the next reviewer cannot tell which requirement was tested. Do not fabricate a photo, measurement or signature.

A deviation is a departure from the applicable requirement or planned process. Record the difference and its impact; seek authorized disposition instead of silently changing the procedure. Depending on the risk, the task may need to pause. Preserve the original evidence and record any correction with traceable history. A failed check can be useful information when it is reported honestly.
lessons.example: The required playback test was not performed because access was unavailable. Record “not tested, access pending,” rather than a pass.
lessons.exercise: Rewrite “all OK” into a test record with an unresolved item.

objectives: Distinguish process prevention from checking a finished result.
explanation: Quality assurance builds reliable methods, training and review into the work. Quality control checks outputs against defined requirements. lessons.title: AI checks and human authority
objectives: Use AI feedback as practice support with source and approval controls.
explanation: An AI can help compare a written report with a checklist, ask missing questions and explain a training example. It may still misunderstand images, omit context or produce an unsupported answer. It cannot verify hidden physical conditions from a photograph, grant approval or turn a draft SOP into company policy.

Before accepting AI feedback, inspect the cited source, version, approval and applicability. Keep company-authoritative retrieval restricted to approved company records. Draft and hypothetical items may support clearly labeled practice, but not a policy answer. Do not submit secrets or unnecessary personal data. An AI practice score is formative feedback; official competency assessment requires the company’s approved human-led process.
